summary: Your first vote is the big one: Days after your oath, {the body} votes on {the question}, and almost everyone is voting one way.
realLife: Four days after being sworn in as the first woman in Congress in 1917, she voted against entering World War I, speaking briefly as she voted, against House rules. The national suffrage group distanced itself; 49 other members also voted no.
gates: A vote on {the question} on the calendar.
choices: vote no and say why, against the rules

branches.then: The group that helped elect you says you set it back.
A member from elsewhere stands up for you, a tie.
Dozens of others vote with you.
